Crawling along wet walls in the darkened caves of the Umbrawells, this large flat millipede, would look unassuming among the many 
other arthropods that infest the tunnels beneath the earth, had it not been for the foot-long pincers that adorn its head. With these 
two impressive lengths of chitin, it clasps onto climbing mollock, piercing their furred hide to inject a neurotoxin that quickly inhibits 
all muscle use, as the insect then drags its prey back into a lightless crevice to feast. Found in most underground systems, the icullus 
often breeds near the dark, acrid water that runs beneath the earth, their black eggs nestled in the warm bacterial mats that feast on 
the sulfur-infused environment.

Encountering Found near the surface of underground 
rivers and lakes, the icullus is a constant nuisance within the 
Umbrawells. Far too many Travelers have fallen senseless when 
stepping too close to an icullus hidden underfoot. Capturing the 
insects requires fresh bait, live or recently slain, as the icullus 
can appear in great numbers once they smell iron tinged blood 
in the air or water.
A membrane skirts around the insect, 
helps it suction onto smooth vertical 
surfaces, as well as retain moisture when 
it travels far from water
While primarily used to manipulate morsels
